name: emberleaf_hollow

rules.units: metres; u left -> right, v into the picture, z up
rules.obstacle_rule: an obstacle (a shape with move) constrains an agent standing on a floor at z when its z range overlaps [z + max_step, z + agent_height]
rules.bounds: hard walls: every edge of the walkable is a wall segment (wall: a face rising, no step-up; lip: a drop, units never fall; bound: out of bounds at the same height). There is no kill plane; if your game knocks units over the lip, treat a unit whose ground falls below kill_z as lost
rules.sight: eye to eye: from eye_height over one floor to eye_height over the other; blocked by the terrain (nav z_cm as a height field) and by every shape with sight whose prism the segment passes through. High ground sees over whatever is lower than its eye
rules.shots: the same from chest_height, against the shapes with shot

levels.name: ground
levels.note: the whole hollow: one level (the knoll's 1.1 m stays under high_ground_z); no deck

colliders.about: shape: circle (u, v, r) | box (u, v, hu, hv half sizes, a = angle of its hu axis from +u toward +v, radians) | seg (u0, v0 to u1, v1, t = half thickness: a capsule). level, z0..z1 (absolute m), move / sight / shot. kind wall / lip / bound are the edges of the walkable height field

nav.about: two layers on one lattice: 'hf' (the height field: ground and terrace) and 'deck'. Cell (i, j) is centred at (u0 + (j + 0.5) * cell, v0 + (i + 0.5) * cell); arrays are row-major (i * nu + j), base64. clear: uint8 clearance in steps of clear_q m (0 = not walkable): an agent of radius r may stand where clear * clear_q >= r. z_cm: int16 ground height (cm) of every cell, walkable or not (LOS uses it as the terrain). surf: uint8 surface (legend) | 8 on ramps. A hf cell's level is 1 where z >= high_ground_z, else 0; ground and terrace cells touch only on ramps. The deck's floor is deck.z(v).

deck.z: no deck on this map: layer 1 is empty

surfaces.note: speed multipliers: the grass a little slower than the trodden dirt

mode.note: team deathmatch to the last unit: no objectives, no capture; the targets are where the fights happen, for AI and for the fairness check

unit_hues.rule: team colours from these hue bands (no map pixel shows them above chroma 0.2); every unit carries a 1 px ink outline and a 1 px light rim (arena/STYLE.md)

chokepoints.name: north lane west of the knoll
north lane east of the knoll

out_of_bounds.rule: everything outside the walkable height field and the deck; walled, no kill plane (rules.kill_z if you add knockback)

visibility.about: pair (a, b) of `points` (u, v, layer) sees each other eye to eye when bit a * n + b of `bits` (packbits, big-endian within a byte) is set; a coarse helper for AI (who can see this square), the exact test is the LOS function

los.terrain: nav.hf.z_cm (sampled every 0.25 m, 5 cm grace, 0.35 m round each end ignored)
los.shapes: colliders with sight (eye to eye) or shot (chest to chest); a seg is tested as its box

projection.screen: sx = x0 + u * ppm;  sy = y0 - (v * sin_el + z * cos_el) * ppm
projection.depth: v * cos_el - z * sin_el (larger is further: draw far first)
projection.grid_xy: x = (u + v) / sqrt 2, y = (v - u) / sqrt 2 (buildings sit square to x, y)

grid.rows: kind[i] is the row at v = v0 + (i + 0.5) * cell, one digit per cell from u0 (legacy v3; the nav is the exact one)

chokepoints.name: north lane west of the knoll
north lane east of the knoll

dimensions.metre grid: 1 m = 51 px across, 47.5 px into the picture, 19.2 px up
dimensions.the fighting ground: 27 x 8.8 m of dirt and cobbles
dimensions.the pond: 10 x 5 m, two small pools 3.4 x 2.2 m
dimensions.red-crowned trees (frame): hero 9.5-10.5 m, standard 6.6-7.8 m, small 4.6-5.6 m, saplings 2.6-3.2 m
dimensions.other cover: two 2.0-2.4 m logs each side of the fight, a 3.2 m trunk on each knoll shoulder, stumps, bushes
dimensions.pebbles: painted, 2-12 cm (1-6 px); no rock bigger than 0.3 m on the map

occluders: occ.json + occ.png: every tree, bush and prop cut out of map.png with its depth d. Draw a cut-out over a unit whose depth is larger (further) than d and whose box it overlaps.
